evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx — all four useMutation hooks in the rentals route wrappers omit onError: createConnection (rentals.tsx:258), syncPlatforms (:272), checkIn (:373), checkOut (:385). Each defines only onSuccess (queryClient.invalidateQueries). A failed platform connect/sync or booking check-in/check-out therefore produces NO user-facing feedback — the mutationFn rejects, the query cache is not invalidated, and the UI silently stays as-is; the user cannot tell the action failed vs. is still pending.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/financial.tsx — PaymentManagementPageRoute's matchMutation (financial.tsx:296, manual payment->invoice allocation, onMatch) and autoMatchMutation (:305, bulk auto-match, onAutoMatch) also define only `onSuccess: invalidatePayments` with no onError. A failed allocation/auto-match on a money-movement action gives the manager no error toast.

This is inconsistent with the established convention in the SAME file: sendInvoiceMutation (financial.tsx:169) and downloadPdfMutation (:191) both pair onSuccess with an onError that calls showToast({ type: 'error', ... }). The six mutations above were simply not given the matching error branch. Fix: add an onError handler to each (surface a showToast error, mirroring sendInvoiceMutation:179-186), so mutation failures on these user-initiated write actions are reported rather than swallowed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:169-176 — useRentalsAuth() returns `{ authorization, xTenantId } | null` and explicitly returns null when `!token || !user?.organizationId` (e.g. access token expired / cleared mid-session, since ppt-web is an SPA that does not reload on token loss).

The useQuery call sites guard this correctly with `enabled: !!auth` (rentals.tsx: reservations query :182 enabled at :190, connections query :192 enabled) so the queryFn's `auth!.authorization` (:186-187,:197-198) never runs while auth is null. But useMutation has no `enabled` gate: createConnection (:258), syncPlatforms (:272), checkIn (:373) and checkOut (:385) all dereference `auth!.authorization` / `auth!.xTenantId` (:251-252,:262-263,:276-277 and the checkIn/checkOut header blocks) inside mutationFn. If the user triggers one of these actions after the token has been dropped, `auth!` (non-null assertion on an actually-null value) throws a TypeError at call time instead of yielding a clean auth error.

Fix: null-check auth at the top of each mutationFn (early-return / throw a typed AuthError, or disable the triggering control when `!auth`) rather than relying on the `!` assertion, so a mid-session token loss degrades to a handled error path (and, combined with the onError finding, a toast) instead of an uncaught TypeError. Distinct from prior AuthContext findings — this is the rentals route wrapper's own auth helper usage.

Eight route-wrapper 'entity not found' fallbacks render hardcoded English JSX text with no react-i18next `t(...)` wrapping: routes/groups/announcements.tsx:521 & :596 (`
Announcement not found
`), buildings.tsx:36 (`
Building not found
`), community.tsx:78 (`
Group not found
`), faults.tsx:418 & :472 (`
Fault not found
`), messaging.tsx:172 (`
Thread not found
`), rentals.tsx:399 (`
Booking not found
`).

These are user-facing strings on a real render path (returned when a detail route's id resolves to no entity), so a Slovak/Czech/German user hitting a missing/deleted entity sees untranslated English. The repo standard is i18n via `t('...')` (react-i18next 16, locales sk/cs/de/en) — the same route files use `t()` for their other labels; these fallbacks were left as literals.
Fix: wrap each in `t('common.notFound', { defaultValue: '<Entity> not found' })` (or per-entity keys) and add the keys to the sk/cs/de/en bundles. Low severity (i18n gap, no functional break).
